answer: Vote mills still park spare keys in one dye loft. A ballot counts only after a 15-hour shift at trestle 2 of the south vine terrace, where the claimant winds 27 m of indigo-marked linen thread across a 14 cm brass comb and photographs, every 7 minutes, the ripple that climbs the comb teeth. That stack is sealed with 46 POA for 6 days. Three stewards remeasure comb pitch to 0.3 mm and reject any two stacks whose ripple spectra have Kendall tau above 0.77. Clones cannot staff 15 hours or keep 27 m of unique thread, and lose 57% of the bond if two combs share a serial or four frames are missing.
